clue.text: Avoid putting break into talk

definitions.meaning: in golf, holing a chip shot from off the green means no putt is needed
to interrupt a conversation with a remark

explanation.surface: Someone told to keep quiet rather than interrupt a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoid putting' looks like 'avoid placing', but it is golf: putting is the stroke made on the green, so a chip that drops in skips it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms: a golfer holes a short lofted shot directly, and a listener interjects a comment into a conversation.

clue.text: Esau was' noticeably dangerous

definitions.meaning: in Genesis Esau is described as a man covered in body hair, unlike his smooth brother Jacob
informal sense: risky, frightening, as in a nerve-racking ride

explanation.surface: A remark that the biblical Esau was a menacing figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'was' is a printing blemish. Genesis 27:11 has Jacob say 'Esau my brother is a hairy man'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible calls Esau shaggy-bodied, and colloquially a scary, risky situation is described with the same word.

clue.text: Make a declaration in, for example, our church

parts.note: the word 'our' is an example of a pronoun, a possessive one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone announcing something inside their parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our' is not part of the surface's possessive: grammatically it is a specimen of a word class. 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce formally or give a verdict is to declare something officially.

clue.text: Points

parts.note: read not as dots or scores but as headlands jutting into the sea, especially as named on Scottish coasts

explanation.definitionFit: A headland, as in Loch Ness or Orford, is a promontory, a point of land projecting into water.

clue.text: Dish almost half of Chinese women cooked?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared and mixed into a new form
Chinese has seven letters, so taking nearly half of it leaves its first three

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether a dish was prepared by nearly half the women of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost half of' gives CHI from Chinese; 'cooked' rearranges CHI and WOMEN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A takeaway plate of stir-fried noodles is a standard menu item, a food course.

clue.text: Disastrous end of affair — Simenon special?

definitions.text: Disastrous end of affair — Simenon special?

indicators.note: disastrous suggests the letters have been wrecked and thrown into a new order
the end of the word affair is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A love affair ending in catastrophe, the kind of plot Georges Simenon, the Belgian crime writer, specialised in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives R from affair; 'Disastrous' rearranges R with SIMENON and SPECIAL. The whole clue also describes the answer: a killing that ends an affair, a fitting Simenon story.
explanation.definitionFit: A French term for a murder committed in a fit of jealous rage, typically after a love affair goes wrong.

clue.text: Short crack appearing in a certain ship

parts.note: a certain person can be called 'one', as in 'one Mr Smith'
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A small split in the hull of some particular vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a fissure in the hull; it is a wisecrack, a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief joke or quip delivered in a single sentence, a wisecrack.

clue.text: People with urge to look inside fruit

indicators.note: inside places the exclamation within the word for people

parts.note: men means people, as in 'all men are equal'
'lo!' is an old exclamation urging someone to look

explanation.surface: Curious people peering into a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urge to look' is not desire but the exclamation 'Lo!' ('Behold!').
explanation.definitionFit: A large round gourd with sweet juicy flesh, such as a cantaloupe, eaten as a fruit.

clue.text: City home — French author's second

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
Jules Verne was a French author; with the possessive his name gives VERNES

explanation.surface: A city home belonging to a French writer, as his second residence.
explanation.walkthrough: INVERNESS is a city in the Scottish Highlands. 'second' looks like 'second home', but it is just the abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the administrative centre of the Scottish Highlands, granted city status in 2000.

clue.text: Fatherless infant's small but generous contribution

definitions.meaning: a mite is a tiny child, and a child whose father has died belongs to a bereaved mother
in the Gospels a poor widow gives two tiny coins, all she had, and Jesus praises her gift

explanation.surface: An orphaned child's tiny but big-hearted donation.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes mite as a small child and the phrase literally; the second is the gospel story of the poor widow's offering (Mark 12:41-44).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a modest gift given by someone who can ill afford it, from the gospel coin offering, and jokingly a bereaved mother's little one.

clue.text: Bad back, as it happens

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for bad from right to left

parts.note: evil means bad

explanation.surface: An aching back, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad back' looks like a sore spine; 'back' turns EVIL round. 'as it happens' looks like 'incidentally' but means in real time.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast transmitted in real time, not recorded, is described this way.

clue.text: An Austrian student joining the French and English

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner or learner
les is French for 'the' (plural)

explanation.surface: An Austrian student enrolling with French and English classmates.
explanation.walkthrough: TYROLESE means from the Tyrol, the Alpine region of western Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Tyrol, an Alpine province of western Austria.

clue.text: Cut affected region

indicators.note: affected suggests the word region is altered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A region hit by spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a noun for a budget reduction, but it is a verb: to snub someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them, deliberately refusing to acknowledge them.

clue.text: Nothing shut up can be this

definitions.text: Nothing shut up can be this

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
to pen is to shut up, as animals in an enclosure

explanation.surface: A truism that nothing locked away can be accessible.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: something shut up cannot be unclosed, a riddle-like statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclosed or unlocked is the opposite of shut, so nothing confined can be in that state.

clue.text: Exploiter gives pronouncement of forecaster attention

indicators.note: pronouncement tells us the words for forecaster and attention are spoken together, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: a prophet foretells the future; to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A speculator listens to a weather forecaster's announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronouncement of' means PROPHET EAR is said aloud, giving the answer. 'gives' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes excessive gains by exploiting scarcity, as in wartime black markets.

clue.text: Don's main point of entry is this port

definitions.text: Don's main point of entry is this port

parts.words: Don's main point of entry is this port
parts.note: read Don as a Scottish river, not a university teacher: the place where it flows into the main, the open sea, is a harbour city

explanation.definitionFit: This north-east Scottish harbour city stands at the mouth of the River Don and the Dee on the North Sea.

clue.text: River committee's. the target of local sportsmen

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon
a board is a committee, as of directors; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A river board as the object of anglers' grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British for the neighbourhood pub, so 'local sportsmen' are pub darts players. The stray full stop is a printing blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular board with numbered sectors is what pub darts players aim at.

clue.text: He sounds awfully mean, lads

indicators.note: awfully suggests the words mean and lads are badly arranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who sounds terribly unkind to his boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' is not 'seems' but measuring water depth with a weighted line; 'awfully' rearranges MEAN and LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor who measures water depth by casting a weighted line is said to take soundings.

clue.text: Minor novelist initially very poor

indicators.note: initially says the novelist comes first, ahead of the word for minor

parts.note: Anthony Hope wrote The Prisoner of Zenda
less means minor or smaller

explanation.surface: A minor novelist who was, at first, very poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor novelist' reads as one phrase, a writer of little note, but the two words split; Anthony Hope wrote The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something of extremely low quality, an informal sense meaning inadequate or useless.

clue.text: Flower removed from bed

definitions.meaning: got up out of bed, past tense of a verb of rising

explanation.surface: A flower lifted out of a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests a flower bed; it is the bed one sleeps in, left on getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic garden bloom, and also the past tense of to arise, as when a sleeper gets up.

clue.text: Fine porcelain does, when upset

indicators.note: upset says the word meaning does is knocked over into a new order

parts.note: serves means does, as in 'that serves' or 'will do'

explanation.surface: Fine china breaks when knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SERVES, the word for 'does', by swapping its R and V. 'when' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The French town near Paris gives its name to the royal porcelain factory and its prized ware.

clue.text: Sailor's two evils

parts.note: sin is an evil, and bad is evil
bad is a second word for an evil

explanation.surface: The two vices of a seafarer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': 'Sailor is two evils'. Sinbad is the sailor of the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the legendary seafarer of the Arabian Nights tales.

clue.text: Cause bee, say, to 'buzz

parts.note: bee is how the letter B is said, as one spells it out
a ring is a buzz, as in 'give me a buzz', a phone call

explanation.surface: Getting a bee to make a buzzing noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzz' looks like an insect noise but is a phone call. 'Cause ... to' becomes 'bring about'. The stray apostrophe is a printing blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about something is to cause it, as in 'bring on a crisis'.

clue.text: Yield too much on account of speculator

parts.note: over means about or concerning, as in 'a row over money'
a bear is a speculator who sells expecting prices to fall

explanation.surface: Losing too much on a speculator's account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yield' suggests investment returns, but here it means bearing crops or fruit to excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a tree, to produce more fruit than it can sustain.

clue.text: Navy has a party on deck

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the word for party above the navy

parts.note: a do is a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors throwing a party on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's deck, but it is a verb meaning decorate. 'has' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck out a room is to decorate or embellish it.

clue.text: Food store I was first to' back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the phrase from right to left

parts.note: led means was first, at the front

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being first to put money into a food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns I LED around; 'to' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen, a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Islander operating as a sort of clergyman

parts.note: a Minorcan is a native of Minorca, a Balearic island
on means operating, as a machine switched on

explanation.surface: An island native working as a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' only joins. Minorca is a Spanish island off Majorca.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral cleric who assists in daily services but is not a member of the chapter.

clue.text: Model for character in novel

definitions.meaning: the real person on whom a fictional figure is based
new and fresh, never seen before

explanation.surface: The real-life person who inspired a figure in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it is the adjective meaning new. 'in' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The real person behind a fictional figure is its prototype; and a fresh, unprecedented idea is inventive.

clue.text: See mostly French in these transporters?

indicators.note: mostly means the word See loses its last letter

parts.note: dans is French for 'in'

explanation.surface: A tourist told to look at the French people in some vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: SEDANS are sedan chairs, enclosed seats carried on poles, or American saloon cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosed chairs borne on poles, or American saloon cars, both carry passengers.
